solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A day in which King becomes King?

indicators.note: 'in which' says the next piece sits inside the phrase just built

parts.note: THUR is the short form of Thursday
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A riddle about a day on which a king turns into a particular, famous king.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'King' is the letter R, set inside A THUR; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary ruler of Camelot is the best-known monarch of British myth.

clue.text: See 19
Figure in reduced claim

indicators.note: 'reduced' says the word for claim loses a letter, here its last

parts.note: to state something is to claim it

explanation.surface: A sum of money cut down in a compensation claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat is short for statistic, a number or figure in a table.

clue.text: Against moving in and out in keyboard part in orchestra

parts.note: CON means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: 'moving' says the two little words that follow are shuffled about

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to people walking in and out during a keyboard player's part in the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns IN and OUT into TINUO.
explanation.definitionFit: Basso continuo is the bass accompaniment, often played on harpsichord, underpinning Baroque orchestral music.

clue.text: Dam river, avoiding damage repeatedly

indicators.note: 'repeatedly' says the shortened piece is written out twice
'avoiding' says the river's letter is kept out of the word for damage

parts.note: to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: An engineer building a dam on a river while taking care not to damage it, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR without R leaves MA, written twice. 'Dam' here is a mother animal, not a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is an animal's mother, and the childish word for a mother suits it.

clue.text: Horn, say, doing for some fortification

parts.note: a horn is an example of a male sheep's body part, so the beast comes first
some of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: Blowing a horn plays its role in a castle's defences.
explanation.walkthrough: A horn is, for example, a ram's part: RAM + PART. 'doing for' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is the broad defensive bank or wall around a fort or castle.

clue.text: Vague term: area in London on heading out, possibly

definitions.text: Vague term: area in London on heading out, possibly

indicators.note: 'Vague' says the letters of the word term are blurred into a new order
'possibly' says the remaining letters may be rearranged
'heading out' says the letters of on leave the city's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A loose name for a district you pass through when leaving London.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM shuffled gives METR; A plus LOND (London losing ON) shuffled gives OLAND. Metroland is the outer suburbs north-west of London served by the Metropolitan line.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is an informal marketing label for commuter suburbs, so it is a vague term for a London area.

clue.text: A long time in servant's servitude

indicators.note: 'in' places the long time inside the servant

parts.note: a page is a young servant; the 's is possessive
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A servant who has spent ages in bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: Peonage is a system of forced labour to pay off debt, a kind of bondage.

clue.text: Rodent study securing trophy, I note

indicators.note: 'securing' means the word for study holds the trophy, I and note inside it

parts.note: to pore over something is to study it
a cup is a typical sporting trophy

explanation.surface: Someone studies the trophy that was won, then makes a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny creature is a large rodent with defensive quills.

clue.text: Undecided, without start or finish

indicators.note: 'without start' says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a pending matter is still undecided

explanation.surface: A tale left undecided, with no beginning or end.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of a story or film is its final part, its conclusion.

clue.text: Upset the old with cut in pension

indicators.note: 'Upset' says the letters are knocked over into a new order
'with cut' says the word old loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An old person upset by a cut in their state pension.
explanation.walkthrough: THE plus OL (old cut short) is upset. 'pension' is the French word for a boarding house, not retirement income.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension in Europe is a small boarding house or guest house offering rooms.

clue.text: I forecast performer turning in almost late

indicators.note: 'in' puts the turned performer inside the shortened word for late
'almost' says the word for late loses its final letter

parts.note: tardy means late

indicators.note: 'turning' says the performer is read backwards

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A late-running performer predicting things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: 'I forecast' is the card talking, not the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune teller lays out cards to predict the future, so the card itself speaks as the predictor.

clue.text: Supports perch, jiggling rear end

indicators.note: 'jiggling rear end' says the last letters are shaken about, the final one moving back a place

parts.note: a roost is a perch for birds
the rear end is the last letter of the word for perch

explanation.surface: A bird on its perch, wiggling its tail, on supporting branches.
explanation.walkthrough: ROOST swaps its last two letters, S and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's roots hold it up and anchor it, just as foundations underpin a building.

clue.text: Dinosaur dung put on after start of irrigation

indicators.note: 'after' means the dung and the putting on follow that letter
'start of' picks the first letter of irrigation

parts.note: guano is bird or bat dung used as fertiliser
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A farmer spreading manure after irrigating the fields.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, one of the first identified.

clue.text: Isle promoting alcohol problems?

definitions.meaning: a lake island in Ireland made famous by Yeats
read as three words, a pub offering everything at no cost would encourage drinking problems

explanation.walkthrough: Split as INN IS FREE, a bar charging nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake Isle of the Yeats poem is a small island in Lough Gill, Ireland.

clue.text: Food expert to finish it up? One tucks into preserve

parts.note: to die is to finish or come to an end

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' says the word it is read from the bottom
'tucks into' says the one goes inside the word for preserve

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nutrition adviser asking if one should finish the jam.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE + TI (IT reversed by 'up') + C(I)AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietician advises on nutrition and diet, making them a specialist in what we eat.

clue.text: Cheers paramour restraining family fool? There should be discussion here

parts.note: TA is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

indicators.note: 'restraining' says the lover holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: a paramour is a lover
kin are one's family
a git is a British insult for a stupid or contemptible person

explanation.surface: Thanking a lover who keeps the family idiot in check, and calling for a proper chat.
explanation.walkthrough: TA + LO(KIN GIT)VER. GIT is British slang for an idiot. It is also a Julian Barnes novel, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Discussing a matter at length is the meaning of the phrase, so a talk is where discussion should happen.

clue.text: Ship left off circling jagged peaks, one recalls

indicators.note: 'circling' says the shortened ship goes round the scrambled mountains
'off' says the letter for left comes away from the ship

parts.note: a keel is an old word for a flat-bottomed barge

indicators.note: 'jagged' says the letters of peaks are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship that has left, sailing around craggy mountain peaks, is something one remembers.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEL, an old word for a barge, loses L; 'one recalls' means a thing one remembers by, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is kept to bring something to mind, so it is a thing by which one remembers.

clue.text: Repeat role involving only half of same?

indicators.note: 'involving' says the word for role contains the next piece

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

indicators.note: 'only half of' says the word keeps just its first two letters of four

parts.note: the same thing as before, the role itself

explanation.surface: An actor asked to repeat a role that is only half the size.
explanation.walkthrough: PA(RO)RT: 'same' points back to the word role, of which half is RO.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat words mechanically without understanding is to mimic them like a talking bird.

clue.text: Recipient's to finish in a river

indicators.note: 'in' puts the finishing word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to dress stone or timber is to give it a finish

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a message to finish off a river project.
explanation.walkthrough: A + D(DRESS)EE. 'Recipient's' reads as 'recipient is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a letter is sent is its receiver.

clue.text: No love for dull escort

indicators.note: 'No' says the following letter for love is taken away

parts.note: boring means dull
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: No romance from a tedious companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone along is to accompany or escort them.

clue.text: Military inventor's wild lawless brain

indicators.note: 'wild' says the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An inventor of weapons described as having an untamed, outlaw mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The engineer devised the bouncing bomb used in the 1943 Dambusters raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The British engineer designed wartime aircraft and bombs, making him a military inventor.

clue.text: Farming monarch feeding last of waste to pig?

indicators.note: 'feeding' says the letter goes inside the word for pig, as food goes in

parts.note: to pig out is to gorge

indicators.note: 'last of' picks the final letter of waste

explanation.surface: A royal farmer giving leftover scraps to the pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: GOR(E)GE. George III was nicknamed 'Farmer George' for his interest in agriculture.
explanation.definitionFit: King George III's nickname came from his keen interest in agriculture.

clue.text: Official's to bring up including key point, right?

indicators.note: 'including' says the key point and right go inside the word for bring up

parts.note: to rear children is to bring them up
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A civil servant asking whether to raise a key matter.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(GIST R)AR; 'Official's' reads as 'official is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar records births, marriages and deaths, a public official.

clue.text: Unpleasant filth cut down

indicators.note: 'cut down' says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: grime is filth or dirt

explanation.surface: Dirt being cleared away is a nasty job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grim is forbidding or disagreeable.

clue.text: Opportune complaint Government ignored

indicators.note: 'ignored' says the letter for Government is left out

parts.note: a gripe is a complaint

explanation.surface: A timely protest the authorities chose to ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: When the time is ripe it is the right moment to act.

clue.text: Greek character keeping in money

indicators.note: 'keeping' says the Greek letter holds the next word inside

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R

explanation.surface: A Greek holding on to cash.
explanation.walkthrough: RH(IN)O. The word is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for cash, of uncertain origin.

clue.text: Water swamping weak, weak light

indicators.note: 'swamping' says the water floods over the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: tinkle is childish slang for urine, so water in that sense

explanation.surface: A flood overwhelming a feeble, flickering lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: T(W)INKLE. 'Water' is urine here, as in 'pass water'.
explanation.definitionFit: A star's glimmer or flicker is a faint, fleeting gleam.

clue.text: Writing one note less about France's European currency once

indicators.note: 'about' says the shortened writing goes round the country's letter
'less' says one note is taken away

parts.note: penning is writing
N is short for note, and only one is removed
F is the international code for France

explanation.surface: Someone writing about the old French currency, short of a note.
explanation.walkthrough: PENNING minus one N, then F slipped in after P.
explanation.definitionFit: The small coin was a hundredth of a German mark before the euro.
